title: Emotional Recognition | The Future With Hannah Fry Episode 2
summary: Cars that can sense anger. Laptops that know if you’re bored. Can a new wave of artificial intelligence really read emotions better than a human? From a Scottish pig farm to the tech mecca of San Francisco, Hannah explores the latest artificial intelligence to figure out if the death of privacy could leave us exposed to greater threats, or if a revolution in online investigative techniques could actually make our societies safer. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wendy’s Shares Jumps On Peltz Bid News
summary: Bloomberg's Matt Monks joins Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg Deals." Shares of Wendy’s jumped to their highest in seven weeks after the Financial Times reported that Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management is preparing a bid to take the struggling fast-food chain private. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Walter Sells Lakers, Seeks Cash to Pay Loans Amid DOJ Probe
summary: Billionaire Mark Walter’s firm is in talks with investors to raise money to help pay down loans on the books of its insurers that had drawn scrutiny from the Justice Department, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Lakers Deal Proves Sports Business Has 'Real Tailwinds'
summary: Kara Nortman, co-founder of Angel City Football Club and managing partner of Monarch Collective, and George Pyne, CEO and founder of Bruin Capital, join Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ancora Comfortable With Its Offer for H.B. Fuller Unit
summary: Ancora Holdings Group is pushing to acquire H.B. Fuller Co.'s building adhesives unit for as much as $1.2 billion. James Chadwick is the president of Ancora's alternatives arm. He says the activist investor is comfortable with the offer and it would be a "win-win" for shareholders. He speaks on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Sweetgreen CEO Says Cyclospora Hurt Sales
summary: Sweetgreen Inc. CEO Jonathan Neman says the cyclospora outbreak had an impact on the business but the US FDA now says it's safe to eat iceberg lettuce again. He says Sweetgreen's supply chain isn’t affected by the cyclospora outbreak and its restaurants don’t serve that kind of lettuce. Neman speaks to Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 'Terrific Tail Winds' In Secondaries: Dawn
summary:
Nigel Dawn, global head of private capital at Evercore, joins Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg Deals." Secondaries deals for private assets surged to a record $121 billion in the first half of 2026, driven by fund managers seeking to hold onto single “trophy” assets longer, according to Evercore.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Americans Have Never Paid This Much for Fuel So Late in The Year
summary: It’s peak driving season in the US, and gasoline and diesel prices have never been this expensive this late in the year.

title: It's A 'Weird Time' For The US Economy, Says Christopher Smart
summary: Christopher Smart, managing partner of Arbroath Group and former special assistant to the President at the National Economic Council under Obama, said that it is a 'weird time' for the US Economy as economic data shows solid numbers, but with weakening growth and geopolitical factors creating uncertainty. Smart said while he's sure the US will need data centers and the investment in AI, he is worried about how making profits on those investments have been pushed further and further down the line.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Stocks Climb Near Record as Earnings Revive Faith in AI Trade

title: Hong, Crowley 'Two Sides of the Same Coin' Says Republican Rep. Steil
summary:
Wisconsin Representative Bryan Steil said that moderate David Crowley and democratic socialist Francesca Hong are 'two sides of the same coin' after Crowley pulled off an upset in the Democratic primary to face Republican Tom Tiffany in the fall. 
Steil said that he expects the race to be close and that he thinks that voters care more about 'kitchen table issues' than 'looking back' at Tiffany's stance on the 2020 election results.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Trades Near 160 Level as Traders Watch for Intervention
summary: The yen held steady near the key level of 160 per dollar on Wednesday, keeping investors on the lookout for more intervention by officials in the foreign-exchange market.

title: EM Currencies Pare Gains as CPI Fails to Shift Fed Bets
summary: Emerging-market currencies gave back most of the advance seen on Wednesday morning as tame US inflation data failed to sway bets that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates at its next meeting.

title: Optical Stocks Soar as Market’s Favorite Momentum Bet Resurfaces
summary: One of the stock market’s favorite momentum plays from earlier this year is re-emerging as rising confidence in artificial intelligence spending sends the shares of optical component makers soaring again.

title: US Sells 10-Year Debt at Highest Yields Since Financial Crisis
summary: A $42 billion auction of 10-year US Treasuries resulted in the highest yield for the benchmark securities since 2007, luring decent appetite from investors who’ve been demanding more compensation to finance the US government.

title: Goldman Sachs to Acquire ETF Provider Neos in $2.3 Billion Deal
summary: Goldman Sachs Group will pay as much as $2.25 billion to buy Neos Investments,  expanding its asset manager’s reach in the actively managed exchange-traded fund market. Bloomberg's Neil Sipes joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Data Center QTS Holds Investor Calls Ahead of Possible Debt Sale
summary: Subsidiaries of QualityTech LP are holding series of fixed income investor calls ahead of a potential bond offering that would add to this year’s surge in technology deals.

title: Yardeni Raises S&P 500 Target on 'Fabulous Earnings Momentum'
summary:
An in-line inflation reading spurred gains in both stocks and bonds, easing concern about imminent Federal Reserve interest-rate increases despite elevated oil prices.
Ed Yardeni, Founder at Yardeni Research, talks about raising his S&P target and the market melt up. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Cava Sales Jump as Americans Flock to Pita Chips, Salmon
summary: Cava is hot, kind of bucking a trend when it comes to eating out with prices generally rising. The fast-casual restaurant chain known for its Mediterranean-inspired dishes says sales rose faster than expected due to increased demand for its salmon and pita chips. Sales did slow down due the cyclospora outbreak. Michael Halen, Bloomberg Intelligence senior restaurant analyst, has more.  (Source: Bloomberg)
